text: The project 'Code a 2D Mobile Game in less than 6 hours' was created by P.J. Paweska.
The project aims to teach participants how to design and code a 2D mobile game using Flame Engine and Flutter.
The funding period for the project was from January 14, 2022, to February 23, 2022.
The project had a funding goal of CA$ 500.
The project received CA$ 1,655 from 27 backers.
The course promises to teach how to code a full mobile game in less than 6 hours.
The project is based in Toronto, Canada.
The project is categorized under the software domain.
The project is hosted on Kickstarter.
The course is designed for game enthusiasts who want to learn how to write mobile games but may lack the time to dedicate to it.
The course is designed for coders who want to create their own mobile game using a 2D engine.
The course aims to take participants from 0 to hero in less than 6 hours.
The Flame Engine is a minimalist 2D game engine that runs on top of the Flutter framework.
The Flame Engine is light-weight with a small footprint, making it suitable for mobile games.
The Flutter framework allows for one code base and multiple platform deployment.
Using the Flutter framework, developers can write once and deploy to both iOS and Android.
The Flutter framework enables developers to create their own GUI from scratch, independent of the specific OS GUI.
The project is a crash course titled 'Code a 2D Mobile Game in less than 6 hours' by P.J. Paweska.

The course teaches 2D game coding through practical case studies.
Each case study provides a full solution to a specific element of 2D game coding, such as joystick control or collision detection.
The game to be developed in the course is the retro-game Asteroids from ATARI.
Asteroids is chosen as it is suitable for learning the fundamentals of a 2D game engine.
Asteroids can be played on both phone and tablet devices.
Participants are assumed to have some coding experience and familiarity with Flutter/Dart.
